title: What is DLT? A Complete Guide to DLT Registration for Bulk SMS in India
description:
By Textora Technologies (TextoraSMS)

In the digital world, SMS is how businesses today can communicate instantly with their customers. From OTPs, order confirmations, payment alerts, appointment reminders to promotional offers, SMS is one of the most effective communication channels. However, to ensure messaging is secure and spam-free, the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) came up with the Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) framework.

If you are planning to send Bulk SMS in India, then DLT is essential. In this guide, we’ll cover what is DLT, why is DLT mandatory, how does DLT work and how Textora Technologies (TextoraSMS) can help your business stay compliant.

What is DLT?

TRAI has introduced DLT (Distributed Ledger Technology), a secure and transparent digital framework to regulate commercial SMS communication in India. It vets businesses before they are allowed to send SMS messages to customers and makes sure that only approved message templates are sent over telecom networks.

DLT's main goal is to stop spam, prevent fraudulent SMS, and build confidence among customers in business communications.

To put it simply, DLT is a verification system that verifies the businesses and their SMS content before the messages are delivered to customers.

Why did DLT come about?

Before DLT businesses and individuals were able to send bulk SMS without any proper verification processes. As a result, there has been an explosion of spam messages, fake bank alerts, phishing attacks and bogus promotions.

To address these issues, TRAI has mandated DLT registration for entities sending commercial SMS. Today telecom operators only deliver SMS from verified entities with approved Sender IDs and message templates.

Why is DLT significant?

The benefits of DLT for both businesses and customers are numerous.

Better Security

DLT fights fraud by ensuring that only verified businesses can send commercial messages.

Improved SMS Delivery

Telecom regulations are met by approved messages, which are more likely to reach customers.

Customer Confidence

Receiving SMS from verified Sender Ids increases customer confidence on the message.

Regulatory Compliance

DLT helps your business to comply with TRAI guidelines and reduces the risk of SMS rejection or blocking.

Brand Security

Your registered Sender ID prevents unauthorised people from using your business name.

How Does DLT Work?

The DLT system provides a systematic verification process before businesses can start sending Bulk SMS.

1. Registration of a business entity

The first step is to register your company on a DLT platform. During registration, businesses upload documents like PAN, GST (if applicable), proof of business address and details of authorised contact person.

The business will be issued a unique Entity ID once verified.

2. Registering the Sender ID (Header)

Sender ID, also called Header, is the business name that is displayed as the sender of the SMS.

For example:

TEXTORA
AMAZON
ICICIB
HDFCBK.

Each Sender ID needs to be approved before you can use it to send SMS.

3. Develop SMS Templates

Businesses must register every type of SMS they intend to send.

For example:

One-time password messages
Verifying Payments
Order updates
Delivery alerts
Promotional offers
Appointment reminders.

Only approved templates are allowed to be sent across telecom networks.

4. Approval of Variable

Registered template can be added Approved variables for dynamic information like customer names, OTPs, order numbers, invoice IDs or tracking numbers.

5. Delivery of Messages

After DLT registration and getting approval for Sender IDs and templates, businesses can send compliant SMS through an authorised Bulk SMS provider.

A well-planned business communication strategy helps ensure that these interactions are timely, relevant, personalized, and useful.

With modern customer communication tools, businesses can communicate with customers across multiple channels while automating repetitive communication and managing large volumes of conversations efficiently.

Understanding Customer Engagement in Modern Business

The Connection Between Customer Communication and Customer Engagement

Customer engagement refers to the ongoing interaction between a business and its customers throughout the complete customer lifecycle.

This lifecycle can include:

Awareness → Interest → Consideration → Purchase → Post-Purchase Support → Retention → Loyalty

Unlike traditional marketing, which often focuses primarily on selling products or services, customer engagement focuses on creating useful and meaningful interactions throughout the customer journey.

Strong customer communication plays an important role in this process.

For example, a customer may receive:

An instant response to an enquiry

A product or service update

An order confirmation

A payment notification

An appointment reminder

A delivery update

A customer support message

A personalized promotional communication

When communication is relevant and timely, customers can find it easier to interact with a business.

For smaller businesses with a limited number of customers, communication can often be handled manually. However, as the customer base grows into hundreds or thousands of customers, manually managing every interaction becomes increasingly difficult.

This is where WhatsApp Business API, Bulk WhatsApp, SMS API, RCS, Email Marketing, Voice SMS, and automation solutions can help businesses manage communication at scale.

Why Customer Engagement Is Critical for Business Growth

Customer engagement can influence several important business outcomes, including:

Customer retention

Repeat purchases

Customer satisfaction

Brand relationships

Referrals

Customer feedback

Sales opportunities

Engaged customers may be more likely to continue interacting with businesses when they receive useful and timely communication.

Effective business communication also helps internal teams manage customer interactions more efficiently.

For example, businesses can use automated communication for routine updates while allowing customer support teams to focus on conversations that require human assistance.

A structured communication strategy combined with suitable customer communication tools can help businesses create a more consistent customer experience.

Common Customer Communication Challenges Businesses Face

Fragmented Communication Channels

Customers may contact a business through WhatsApp, SMS, email, phone calls, social media, or a website.

When these channels are managed separately, businesses may struggle to maintain consistent communication and track customer conversations.

Integrated communication solutions can help businesses organize communication more efficiently.

Slow Response Times

Customers often expect quick responses to enquiries.

If a potential customer sends a message and receives a response much later, the business may lose an opportunity to continue the conversation.

Automated replies, notifications, and workflows can help businesses acknowledge customer enquiries quickly.

Lack of Personalization

Generic communication may not always be relevant to customers.

Businesses can use customer information and communication history to create more relevant messages, such as personalized order updates, recommendations, reminders, or follow-ups.

Disconnected Internal Teams

When sales, marketing, and support teams operate using different communication systems, customer information can become fragmented.

Centralized communication platforms can help teams access relevant customer information and maintain more consistent communication.

Examples include:

Generating leads

Improving customer support

Increasing repeat purchases

Sending transaction updates

Improving customer retention
